hook.line: Sooner or later someone says "you said it was urgent!" and you need to answer "I never said that". In Spanish that little *no* changes the verb that follows, and getting it right makes you sound precise instead of defensive.
hook.en: I didn't say it was urgent.

examples.es: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
examples.en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.
He didn't say it was urgent.
I saw that Vale was angry.

examples.es: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada.
examples.en: I didn't see that Vale was angry.

examples.es: No oí que sonara el teléfono.
examples.en: I didn't hear the phone ring.

rule:
After *vi que*, *oí que* or *dijo que*, you use the ordinary past verb: *Vi que Vale estaba enojada.* *Dijo que era urgente.* You are vouching for it.

Put *no* in front and you are no longer vouching, so the verb after *que* switches to the past form that ends in *-ra*: *estaba* becomes *estuviera*, *era* becomes *fuera*, *tenía* becomes *tuviera*, *llegó* becomes *llegara*, *sonó* becomes *sonara*.

*No vi que estuviera enojada.* *No dijo que fuera urgente.* It is the same switch as after *no creo que*.

So does *No es que no quiera, es que no puedo*: the first half is the thing you deny.

English keeps one verb for both. Spanish changes it.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after negated verbs of perception and speech: the *no* turns a fact into a claim you don't back.

yourTurn.prompt: I didn't say it was urgent. Choose *fuera* or *era*: No dije que ___ urgente.
yourTurn.why: After *no dije que* the verb takes the *-ra* form: *fuera*.

yourTurn.prompt: I saw that Vale was angry. Choose *estaba* or *estuviera*: Vi que Vale ___ enojada.
yourTurn.why: With no *no*, you are vouching for it, so the ordinary past is *estaba*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't see that Vale was angry.
yourTurn.answer: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada.
accept: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't hear the phone ring.
yourTurn.answer: No oí que sonara el teléfono.
accept: No oí que sonara el teléfono
No oí que el teléfono sonara.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: He didn't say it was urgent.
Make it negative: Dijo que Vale tenía la culpa.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Vi que llegaba Hernando.
Say: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.
yourTurn.answer: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
accept: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo
yourTurn.why: The denied half takes *quiera*; the true half stays ordinary: *puedo*.

pitfalls.wrong: No vi que Vale estaba enojada.
pitfalls.right: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *no vi que* the verb steps back into the *-ra* form.
Almost. Once *dijo* is negated, you use *fuera*, not *era*.
Almost. A denied sighting takes the *-ra* form: *llegara*.
Almost. Without *no* you are reporting what you saw, so use the ordinary past.
